Deviations from the sketch, on purpose: section guesses live in a keyword table in code (SectionKeywords) with per-household corrections in shopping_section_overrides, rather than a seeded ingredient_section_seed table — a seed that ships in a migration cannot be corrected without another migration. Hand-written service worker on SvelteKit's $service-worker instead of @vite-pwa/sveltekit: no svelte.config.js in this project, injectManifest semantics come free, and the file is short enough to read. Precaches the shell per build, answers navigations from cache, never caches /api, and defers skipWaiting to a culina:activate message from the page with a non-expiring update toast. Covered by tests/e2e/pwa.spec.ts and src/lib/app/updates.spec.ts. Install prompt verified against the manifest; Lighthouse run deferred to the packaged container.

A recipe that has been opened stays readable and cookable offline: allow-listed stale-while-revalidate for the recipe, cache-first for its image, network-first for the list, plus /users/me so a cold offline start can tell 'offline' from 'signed out'. Cleared on sign-in and sign-out. Offline badge in the shell and client-side failures now speak the reader's language via $shell/explain. Deviation from the sketch: mutating controls are not disabled offline — they stay tappable and the app says 'You are offline. This will be possible again when you reconnect.' A disabled control with no explanation is worse than a control that explains itself, and the editor keeps its draft either way. Covered by tests/e2e/pwa.spec.ts.

Three-stage Dockerfile at the repo root. Built, run against a real database, and verified: migrations applied at boot, /health/ready 200, the SPA served at / and on a deep link, the service worker served no-cache, and Docker reporting the container healthy. 197 MB against the ~250 MB target. Two things the bead did not anticipate: NuGet lock files did not exist, so RestorePackagesWithLockFile is now on (excluded for the .slnx, which has no target framework and makes NuGet refuse the restore); and the chiseled runtime has no shell or curl, so the HEALTHCHECK is the app itself — Api --health-check makes one request to /health/ready and exits 0 or 1, the same pattern as --export-openapi. The root .editorconfig has to be in the build context: EnforceCodeStyleInBuild plus warnings-as-errors makes a missing one a failed build.

compose.prod.yaml layers over compose.yaml: database port removed (!override []), read_only with tmpfs /tmp, no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, named volumes for /data/images and /data/keys with a loud comment on each, depends_on service_healthy, and the image's own --health-check. Verified from an empty volume: db healthy, app healthy, migrations 0001-0006 applied, deep link served, first account created. Removed the fixed container_name from both files — it made the compose files unusable for two projects at once, which is exactly the situation when checking a production compose against a running development one. .env.example gained ForwardedHeaders__KnownNetworks.

The premise was already broken: a release build contained the whole gallery, for two independent reasons (import.meta.env.VITE_GALLERY is not substituted when unset, so the condition was a runtime read; and even as a folded constant, Svelte's hoisted templates survive an unreachable {#if}). Fixed with a define'd __CULINA_GALLERY__ literal plus build-tools/gallery.ts, a pre-enforced Vite plugin that swaps the gallery components for empty ones before compilation. pnpm verify:release searches the build for four gallery-only strings; CI runs it after a plain build, and it was verified to fail against a VITE_GALLERY=1 build.

Deviation: no video retained on failure (traces and screenshots are), and the suite runs against the vite preview server proxying to the container rather than against the container's own SPA — the same build either way.

Three arithmetic defects fixed and pinned by fixtures: fractional counts below one are kept (¼ floor) instead of being promoted to 1; scaling to an amount preserves the exact factor and rounds only the serving label; non-finite and non-positive yields can no longer produce a NaN factor. ScaledQuantity now carries the exact value alongside the rounded one. docs/scaling-rules.md reconciled, including removing the never-implemented 'small spoon becomes a pinch' rule. Backend verified to agree: an anchored 7.4-serving add contributes exactly 370 g. No UI rounding feeds into domain amounts — the shopping list is scaled server-side from base amounts.

ASVS 5.0 L2 review recorded in docs/security-review.md with per-requirement evidence, exceptions (no account recovery, no MFA, no audit trail) and owner; no certification claimed. Two defects found and fixed: uploaded photographs were served back with their EXIF, including GPS; and the pixel cap ran after a full decode, so a decompression bomb was decoded before being refused. New tests cover cross-household read and write isolation with real identifiers, stale membership, immediate session revocation from another device, invitation expiry, and that no request body, header or query string is ever logged.

Update offers now wait for a safe moment ($shell/busy, held by the cook screen and the editor), covered by unit tests verified to fail without it. Shared-device case covered end to end: first person's cached reads are gone once the second signs in. Offline limits documented honestly in docs/operations.md and recorded in docs/security-review.md, including the one that cannot be met — a disconnected device cannot learn about revocation. Deliberate deviations: no 'Available offline' badge, no per-recipe removal and no shared-device opt-in were built, because the app makes no offline claim to a person beyond what it does, and adding a downloads manager is a feature rather than a correction. Caching stays keyed by URL within a narrow allow-list rather than by user id: reads are network-first, the store is cleared on sign-in as well as sign-out, and an offline stranger cannot sign in at all.

Edits are journalled to localStorage before sending, keyed by account and recipe, cleared on a successful save and on sign-out; the save indicator distinguishes 'Saved' (the server has it) from 'Kept on this device'. A 412 conflict now offers keep-mine or take-theirs rather than a message and a trap — the journal would otherwise resurface the local version on every reload. Autosave already serialised writes (inFlight + owed), so out-of-order responses were not possible; verified rather than assumed. docs/api.md records the no-retry-on-412 contract. Deliberate deviation: no side-by-side snapshot diff — the two choices are offered, not a merge UI, and the raw ingredient line is preserved by the parser rather than stored separately.

Timers already used absolute deadlines in localStorage and the wake lock was already feature-detected and reacquired on visibilitychange — verified rather than assumed. Fixed: the displayed remaining time was only as fresh as the last interval tick, which a backgrounded tab throttles, so the clock is now re-read on foreground (test verified to fail without it). Step controls raised to the 56px control size. CurrentStepIndex clamped so an edited recipe cannot blank the screen. Deliberate deviations, both documented in docs/domain-model.md: no notification-backed alarm for a closed app, and no step-identity in the cook session — the second is a migration for a rare, immediately visible case.

scripts/restore-rehearsal.sh is the evidence: clean instance, seeded data, three backups, every volume destroyed, restored, and five checks including authorized and unauthorized image access. Passing, in 8s on a laptop. It found a real defect on its first run — the data volumes arrived owned by root, so a fresh instance returned 500 on every photo upload; fixed by creating the directories in the build stage and copying them in with the runtime user's ownership. Backup retention, encryption, access and what to alert on are documented, as is what makes rollback safe (each point naming its test). Closed while culina-v2-hxh (portable export) is still open on purpose: recovery from a backup and portability of an export are different promises, and this bead is the first one. Migrations against a previous release have nothing to test against until the first tag; the checklist for it is written down.

All six contracts verified, each producing at least one real defect: scaling that changed what somebody cooks, uploads that carried a photograph's GPS and decoded a bomb before refusing it, an editor that lost work to a reload, an update offer that interrupted somebody at a hob, a timer stale on unlocking, and a fresh instance that could not accept a photograph at all. Evidence is executable throughout; deliberate absences are recorded in docs/security-review.md, docs/domain-model.md and each bead's close note.

Not done, and recorded rather than skipped: no VoiceOver/NVDA pass (nothing automated substitutes for it), no Lighthouse score (its constituent measurements are checked directly, and a score from a plugged-in laptop means little), and no throttled-connection image budget (needs a device lab). One known flake is documented rather than retried away.
